inputs.notes: Updated for FY2026 actuals (year ended 31 March 2026, announced 22 May 2026). Net debt fell $121.4m to $506.7m (gearing 30.1%, low end of 30-35% target) after record ORA receipts ($336.2m) and $51.1m of divestments. last_fcf is Normalised FCF from Operations (Underlying EBITDA $97.4m minus maintenance capex ~$23m, cash interest ~$26.5m, cash tax ~$4m). Reported FCF (after development capex) was a $(15.0)m outflow ex one-offs in FY26, improved 64% from FY25 $(41.7)m; management targets positive operating FCF in FY27. Fiscal year ends 31 March.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported NPAT collapsed to $0.1m in FY26 (FY25 $30.4m) purely because the non-cash fair value gain on investment property fell to $32.8m from $90.2m, plus $4.6m Holidays Act remediation and $2.1m restructure. Underlying EBITDA (the operating measure) actually grew 13% to $97.4m, and Underlying NPAT grew to $63.7m from $52.5m. EPS and reported-NPAT CAGRs are not meaningful for OCA due to fair value volatility. Underlying EBITDA 3yr CAGR (8.21%, FY2023-FY2026) used as the representative operating trajectory.
historical_growth.notes: FY2021 was a 10-month period (balance date change from May to March) and is excluded from CAGR calculations. Underlying EBITDA: FY2023 $80.0m -> FY2026 $97.4m. 5yr period FY2021(10mo-adj)/FY2022 baseline. ORA receipts grew 14% to a record $336.2m in FY26, driving OCF to $169.4m (+54%).

base.description: Continued recovery and execution. Full $20.4m cost-out programme flows through by FY27 (only $13.2m realised in FY26). Care premiumisation continues (Care Underlying EBITDA per occupied bed already +40% to $27.2k). Record sales cadence sustained; The Helier care residences (53% occupied/under application) and remaining unsold stock sell down through FY27. Gearing held at the low end of the 30-35% range, with falling RBNZ OCR reducing interest costs. Development restarts toward the 150 units/yr target from FY27-28. Operating FCF turns positive in FY27.

bull.description: Strong execution. All $20.4m savings flowing by FY27; care EBITDA per bed continues toward the upper range ($26k-$52k EBITDAR observed across sites). NZ property recovery lifts ORA prices 5-9% p.a. (FY26 already +9% on new sales). Development ramps to 150 units/yr from FY27 at ~40% care-suite development margin. Divestment proceeds and record ORA receipts cut debt faster, gearing toward ~27%. RBNZ cuts reduce financing costs meaningfully; dividends resume FY27 attracting income buyers and supporting a re-rating toward NTA ($1.62).

bear.description: Weak execution. NZ property market stalls, suppressing ORA demand, resales and development margins. The Helier care residences and remaining premium stock sell slowly, delaying further debt reduction. Government aged-care funding lags cost inflation. Cost savings partially offset by revenue headwinds. Development deferred. Retirement Villages Act reform (mandatory buyback) raises working capital needs. Even so, the FY26 deleveraging (net debt $507m, gearing 30.1%) removes the prior covenant/wipeout risk - the bear equity value is now modestly positive rather than negative.

sensitivity.notes: Intrinsic value per share (NZD) for base-case FCF projections across WACC and terminal growth. At base WACC 9% / TG 3.0% intrinsic value is $0.90 vs current price $0.76. The FY26 deleveraging ($113m lower net debt vs prior valuation) reduces the model's sensitivity to WACC versus the prior year, though leverage still matters: a $100m change in net debt moves intrinsic value by ~$0.14/share.

probability_weighted.commentary: Probability-weighted intrinsic value of $0.88 sits ~16% above the current price of $0.76, suggesting modest undervaluation on a pure normalised-FCF basis. The most important change from the prior (H1-FY2026) valuation is the balance sheet: net debt fell $121m to $507m and gearing to 30.1% (low end of target), which lifts equity value and, critically, turns the bear-case equity value modestly positive ($0.14/sh) rather than the prior $(0.07) wipeout. Range of outcomes ($0.14 to $1.60) still reflects an execution-and-property-cycle dependent recovery, but the downside is materially de-risked.

sanity_check.interest_cover_fy26_note: ICR comfortably above the 2.0x covenant minimum after interest costs fell with lower drawn debt and OCR cuts.
sanity_check.fcf_dcf_vs_asset_value_caveat: IMPORTANT: a pure normalised-FCF DCF UNDERSTATES OCA's value. Oceania is a retirement-village/aged-care operator whose value is dominated by property assets - over 90% of the $3.08bn total assets are property, carried at fair value, and NTA per share is $1.62 versus a share price of $0.76 (a 53% discount to NTA) and a base DCF intrinsic value of $0.90. The DCF treats development capex as growth investment and only values the existing portfolio's recurring cash generation as a going concern, capturing none of the land-bank/development pipeline value (~1,270-unit pipeline) and ignoring the embedded ORA float and asset realisation optionality. A liquidation/embedded-value or sum-of-the-parts (NTA-anchored) view yields a materially higher number than the FCF DCF. The DCF therefore should be read as a conservative going-concern floor; the wide gap to NTA is the key valuation tension and the source of re-rating optionality if FCF and dividends are restored in FY27.
sanity_check.verdict: Base DCF $0.90 (+18%) and prob-weighted $0.88 (+16%) both above current $0.76; NTA $1.62 implies far larger asset-backed upside. Cross-checks consistent: modest undervaluation on cash flow, deep discount on assets, downside de-risked by FY26 deleveraging.

dcf_methodology_notes.fcf_approach: Uses Normalised FCF from Operations = Underlying EBITDA minus maintenance capex, cash interest and cash tax. Reported FCF (after development capex) was a $(15.0)m outflow ex one-offs in FY26 and is NOT the DCF input - development capex is growth investment generating future ORA receipts (a record $336.2m in FY26), not a recurring cost.
dcf_methodology_notes.wacc_rationale: Base WACC 9%: NZ risk-free ~4.0%, equity risk premium ~5%, sector beta ~0.9, plus a size/illiquidity premium. Bear 11% reflects residual leverage and execution risk; bull 8.5% reflects the de-risked balance sheet. 8-12% tested in sensitivity.
dcf_methodology_notes.terminal_growth_rationale: Base 3.0% = NZ nominal GDP (~2.5%) plus demographic volume growth (75+ cohort almost doubling by ~2050). Bull 3.5% for accelerating demand; bear 2.5% if property and funding stay soft.
dcf_methodology_notes.net_debt_treatment: Net debt $506.7m deducted from EV. Down $121.4m year-on-year after record ORA receipts and $51.1m divestments - the single biggest driver of the improved equity value and bear-case downside versus the prior valuation.
dcf_methodology_notes.development_capex_excluded: Development capex excluded from normalised FCF; the DCF values the existing portfolio as a going concern. The ~1,270-unit development pipeline and land bank create additional value not modelled here (see sanity_check asset-value caveat).
dcf_methodology_notes.fy2021_exclusion: FY2021 was a 10-month period (balance date change May->March) and is excluded from CAGR calculations.
